K-Means Clustering: Examples and Exercises

This file contains 7 different examples of K-Means Clustering implementation,
demonstrating clustering, evaluation, tuning, validation, and model analysis.
Plus 10 exercises for practice.

Author: ML Curriculum
Date: 2024

sections.title: Example 1: Basic K-Means Clustering
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 1: Basic K-Means Clustering")
print("-" * 60)

# Generate synthetic data with clear clusters
np.random.seed(42)
n_samples = 300
n_features = 2
n_clusters = 3

X, true_labels = make_blobs(
    n_samples=n_samples,
    n_features=n_features,
    centers=n_clusters,
    cluster_std=1.0,
    random_state=42,
)

print(f"Dataset shape: {X.shape}")
print(f"Number of clusters: {n_clusters}")

# Basic K-Means clustering
kmeans_basic = KMeans(
    n_clusters=n_clusters, init="k-means++", n_init=10, max_iter=300, random_state=42
)

kmeans_basic.fit(X)
labels = kmeans_basic.labels_
centroids = kmeans_basic.cluster_centers_
inertia = kmeans_basic.inertia_

print(f"\nK-Means Results:")
print(f"Number of iterations: {kmeans_basic.n_iter_}")
print(f"Inertia (WCSS): {inertia:.4f}")
print(f"Centroids shape: {centroids.shape}")

# Evaluation metrics
silhouette_avg = silhouette_score(X, labels)
calinski_avg = calinski_harabasz_score(X, labels)
davies_avg = davies_bouldin_score(X, labels)

print(f"\nEvaluation Metrics:")
print(f"Silhouette Score: {silhouette_avg:.4f}")
print(f"Calinski-Harabasz Index: {calinski_avg:.4f}")
print(f"Davies-Bouldin Index: {davies_avg:.4f}")

# Cluster analysis
unique_labels = np.unique(labels)
print(f"\nCluster Analysis:")
for label in unique_labels:
    cluster_size = np.sum(labels == label)
    cluster_percentage = (cluster_size / len(labels)) * 100
    print(f"Cluster {label}: {cluster_size} points ({cluster_percentage:.1f}%)")

joblib.dump(kmeans_basic, "models/kmeans_example1_basic.pkl")
print("Basic K-Means model saved to: models/")
```

sections.title: Example 2: K-Means with Different Initialization Methods
sections.body:
```python
print("\n\nExample 2: K-Means with Different Initialization Methods")
print("-" * 70)

# Generate data for comparison
np.random.seed(42)
X_comp = make_blobs(n_samples=500, n_features=2, centers=4, random_state=42)[0]

# Compare different initialization methods
init_methods = ["k-means++", "random"]
results = {}

print("Comparing Initialization Methods:")
print("-" * 50)
print(f"{'Method':<15s} {'Inertia':<12s} {'Silhouette':<12s} {'Iterations':<12s}")
print("-" * 50)

for method in init_methods:
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, init=method, n_init=10, max_iter=300, random_state=42)

    kmeans.fit(X_comp)
    labels = kmeans.labels_

    inertia = kmeans.inertia_
    silhouette = silhouette_score(X_comp, labels)
    iterations = kmeans.n_iter_

    results[method] = {
        "inertia": inertia,
        "silhouette": silhouette,
        "iterations": iterations,
        "model": kmeans,
    }

    print(f"{method:<15s} {inertia:<12.4f} {silhouette:<12.4f} {iterations:<12d}")

best_method = min(results.keys(), key=lambda x: results[x]["inertia"])
print(f"\nBest method (lowest inertia): {best_method}")

joblib.dump(results[best_method]["model"], "models/kmeans_example2_best_init.pkl")
print(f"Best model ({best_method}) saved to: models/")
```

sections.title: Example 3: Finding Optimal K using Elbow Method
sections.body:
```python
print("\n\nExample 3: Finding Optimal K using Elbow Method")
print("-" * 70)

# Generate data for K selection
np.random.seed(42)
X_kselect = make_blobs(n_samples=600, n_features=2, centers=5, random_state=42)[0]

# Test different values of K
k_range = range(1, 11)
inertias = []
silhouette_scores = []

print("Testing different values of K:")
print("-" * 40)
print(f"{'K':<5s} {'Inertia':<12s} {'Silhouette':<12s}")
print("-" * 40)

for k in k_range:
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=k, init="k-means++", n_init=10, random_state=42)

    kmeans.fit(X_kselect)
    labels = kmeans.labels_

    inertias.append(kmeans.inertia_)

    if k > 1:  # Silhouette score requires at least 2 clusters
        silhouette = silhouette_score(X_kselect, labels)
        silhouette_scores.append(silhouette)
    else:
        silhouette_scores.append(0)

    print(f"{k:<5d} {kmeans.inertia_:<12.4f} {silhouette:<12.4f}")

# Find optimal K using elbow method (simplified)
optimal_k_elbow = 5  # Based on the data generation
optimal_k_silhouette = k_range[np.argmax(silhouette_scores[1:]) + 1]

print(f"\nOptimal K (Elbow method): {optimal_k_elbow}")
print(f"Optimal K (Silhouette method): {optimal_k_silhouette}")

# Train model with optimal K
optimal_kmeans = KMeans(
    n_clusters=optimal_k_elbow, init="k-means++", n_init=10, random_state=42
)
optimal_kmeans.fit(X_kselect)

joblib.dump(optimal_kmeans, "models/kmeans_example3_optimal_k.pkl")
print("Optimal K-Means model saved to: models/")
```

sections.title: Example 4: K-Means with Feature Scaling
sections.body:
```python
print("\n\nExample 4: K-Means with Feature Scaling")
print("-" * 70)

# Generate data with different scales
np.random.seed(42)
n_samples = 400

# Create features with different scales
feature1 = np.random.normal(0, 1, n_samples)  # Scale ~1
feature2 = np.random.normal(0, 100, n_samples)  # Scale ~100
feature3 = np.random.normal(0, 0.01, n_samples)  # Scale ~0.01

X_unscaled = np.column_stack([feature1, feature2, feature3])

# Add some clustering structure
X_unscaled[:100, 0] += 5
X_unscaled[100:200, 1] += 200
X_unscaled[200:300, 2] += 0.05

print("Feature scales before scaling:")
print(
    f"Feature 1: mean={X_unscaled[:, 0].mean():.4f}, std={X_unscaled[:, 0].std():.4f}"
)
print(
    f"Feature 2: mean={X_unscaled[:, 1].mean():.4f}, std={X_unscaled[:, 1].std():.4f}"
)
print(
    f"Feature 3: mean={X_unscaled[:, 2].mean():.4f}, std={X_unscaled[:, 2].std():.4f}"
)

# K-Means without scaling
kmeans_unscaled = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42)
kmeans_unscaled.fit(X_unscaled)
labels_unscaled = kmeans_unscaled.labels_

# K-Means with scaling
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_unscaled)

kmeans_scaled = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42)
kmeans_scaled.fit(X_scaled)
labels_scaled = kmeans_scaled.labels_

print(f"\nFeature scales after scaling:")
print(f"Feature 1: mean={X_scaled[:, 0].mean():.4f}, std={X_scaled[:, 0].std():.4f}")
print(f"Feature 2: mean={X_scaled[:, 1].mean():.4f}, std={X_scaled[:, 1].std():.4f}")
print(f"Feature 3: mean={X_scaled[:, 2].mean():.4f}, std={X_scaled[:, 2].std():.4f}")

# Compare results
print(f"\nComparison of Results:")
print("-" * 50)
print(f"{'Method':<15s} {'Inertia':<12s} {'Silhouette':<12s}")
print("-" * 50)

inertia_unscaled = kmeans_unscaled.inertia_
silhouette_unscaled = silhouette_score(X_unscaled, labels_unscaled)
print(f"{'Unscaled':<15s} {inertia_unscaled:<12.4f} {silhouette_unscaled:<12.4f}")

inertia_scaled = kmeans_scaled.inertia_
silhouette_scaled = silhouette_score(X_scaled, labels_scaled)
print(f"{'Scaled':<15s} {inertia_scaled:<12.4f} {silhouette_scaled:<12.4f}")

joblib.dump(kmeans_scaled, "models/kmeans_example4_scaled.pkl")
print("Scaled K-Means model saved to: models/")
```

sections.title: Example 5: Mini-Batch K-Means for Large Datasets
sections.body:
```python
print("\n\nExample 5: Mini-Batch K-Means for Large Datasets")
print("-" * 70)

# Generate larger dataset
np.random.seed(42)
X_large = make_blobs(n_samples=10000, n_features=2, centers=4, random_state=42)[0]

print(f"Large dataset shape: {X_large.shape}")

# Regular K-Means
kmeans_regular = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42)
kmeans_regular.fit(X_large)
labels_regular = kmeans_regular.labels_

# Mini-Batch K-Means
minibatch_kmeans = MiniBatchKMeans(n_clusters=4, batch_size=1000, random_state=42)
minibatch_kmeans.fit(X_large)
labels_minibatch = minibatch_kmeans.labels_

print(f"\nComparison of K-Means vs Mini-Batch K-Means:")
print("-" * 60)
print(f"{'Method':<20s} {'Inertia':<12s} {'Silhouette':<12s} {'Time (s)':<10s}")
print("-" * 60)

import time

# Regular K-Means timing
start_time = time.time()
kmeans_regular.fit(X_large)
regular_time = time.time() - start_time

regular_inertia = kmeans_regular.inertia_
regular_silhouette = silhouette_score(X_large, labels_regular)
print(
    f"{'Regular K-Means':<20s} {regular_inertia:<12.4f} {regular_silhouette:<12.4f} {regular_time:<10.4f}"
)

# Mini-Batch K-Means timing
start_time = time.time()
minibatch_kmeans.fit(X_large)
minibatch_time = time.time() - start_time

minibatch_inertia = minibatch_kmeans.inertia_
minibatch_silhouette = silhouette_score(X_large, labels_minibatch)
print(
    f"{'Mini-Batch K-Means':<20s} {minibatch_inertia:<12.4f} {minibatch_silhouette:<12.4f} {minibatch_time:<10.4f}"
)

print(f"\nSpeed improvement: {regular_time/minibatch_time:.2f}x faster")

joblib.dump(minibatch_kmeans, "models/kmeans_example5_minibatch.pkl")
print("Mini-Batch K-Means model saved to: models/")
```

sections.title: Example 6: K-Means Limitations and Challenges
sections.body:
```python
print("\n\nExample 6: K-Means Limitations and Challenges")
print("-" * 70)

# Generate challenging datasets
np.random.seed(42)

# Dataset 1: Non-spherical clusters (moons)
X_moons, _ = make_moons(n_samples=300, noise=0.1, random_state=42)

# Dataset 2: Concentric circles
X_circles, _ = make_circles(n_samples=300, noise=0.1, factor=0.5, random_state=42)

# Dataset 3: Uneven cluster sizes
X_uneven = make_blobs(n_samples=[50, 200, 50], centers=3, random_state=42)[0]

datasets = {"Moons": X_moons, "Circles": X_circles, "Uneven": X_uneven}

print("K-Means Performance on Challenging Datasets:")
print("-" * 70)
print(
    f"{'Dataset':<12s} {'K':<5s} {'Inertia':<12s} {'Silhouette':<12s} {'Comment':<20s}"
)
print("-" * 70)

for name, X_data in datasets.items():
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=2, random_state=42)
    kmeans.fit(X_data)
    labels = kmeans.labels_

    inertia = kmeans.inertia_
    silhouette = silhouette_score(X_data, labels)

    if name == "Moons":
        comment = "Non-spherical shapes"
    elif name == "Circles":
        comment = "Concentric circles"
    else:
        comment = "Uneven sizes"

    print(f"{name:<12s} {2:<5d} {inertia:<12.4f} {silhouette:<12.4f} {comment:<20s}")

print(f"\nKey Limitations Demonstrated:")
print("- K-Means assumes spherical clusters")
print("- K-Means assumes similar cluster sizes")
print("- K-Means requires specifying K")
print("- K-Means is sensitive to initialization")
```

sections.title: Example 7: Comprehensive K-Means Analysis
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Test multiple K values
- Find best K based on different metrics
- Use consensus K (most common)

```python
print("\n\nExample 7: Comprehensive K-Means Analysis")
print("-" * 70)

# Generate comprehensive dataset
np.random.seed(42)
X_comprehensive = make_blobs(
    n_samples=800, n_features=3, centers=4, cluster_std=1.5, random_state=42
)[0]

# Add some noise
X_comprehensive += np.random.normal(0, 0.1, X_comprehensive.shape)

print(f"Comprehensive dataset shape: {X_comprehensive.shape}")

# Scale the data
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_comprehensive_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_comprehensive)

# Test multiple K values
k_values = range(2, 11)
results_comprehensive = {}

print("Comprehensive K-Means Analysis:")
print("-" * 70)
print(
    f"{'K':<5s} {'Inertia':<12s} {'Silhouette':<12s} {'Calinski':<12s} {'Davies':<12s}"
)
print("-" * 70)

for k in k_values:
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=k, init="k-means++", n_init=20, random_state=42)

    kmeans.fit(X_comprehensive_scaled)
    labels = kmeans.labels_

    inertia = kmeans.inertia_
    silhouette = silhouette_score(X_comprehensive_scaled, labels)
    calinski = calinski_harabasz_score(X_comprehensive_scaled, labels)
    davies = davies_bouldin_score(X_comprehensive_scaled, labels)

    results_comprehensive[k] = {
        "inertia": inertia,
        "silhouette": silhouette,
        "calinski": calinski,
        "davies": davies,
        "model": kmeans,
    }

    print(
        f"{k:<5d} {inertia:<12.4f} {silhouette:<12.4f} {calinski:<12.4f} {davies:<12.4f}"
    )

# Find best K based on different metrics
best_k_silhouette = max(k_values, key=lambda k: results_comprehensive[k]["silhouette"])
best_k_calinski = max(k_values, key=lambda k: results_comprehensive[k]["calinski"])
best_k_davies = min(k_values, key=lambda k: results_comprehensive[k]["davies"])

print(f"\nBest K based on different metrics:")
print(f"Silhouette Score: K = {best_k_silhouette}")
print(f"Calinski-Harabasz: K = {best_k_calinski}")
print(f"Davies-Bouldin: K = {best_k_davies}")

# Use consensus K (most common)
consensus_k = best_k_silhouette  # Using silhouette as primary metric
best_model = results_comprehensive[consensus_k]["model"]

print(f"\nSelected K: {consensus_k}")

# Final model analysis
final_labels = best_model.labels_
final_centroids = best_model.cluster_centers_

print(f"\nFinal Model Analysis:")
print(f"Number of iterations: {best_model.n_iter_}")
print(f"Final inertia: {best_model.inertia_:.4f}")

# Cluster analysis
unique_labels = np.unique(final_labels)
print(f"\nCluster Distribution:")
for label in unique_labels:
    cluster_size = np.sum(final_labels == label)
    cluster_percentage = (cluster_size / len(final_labels)) * 100
    print(f"Cluster {label}: {cluster_size} points ({cluster_percentage:.1f}%)")

joblib.dump(best_model, "models/kmeans_example7_comprehensive.pkl")
print("Comprehensive K-Means model saved to: models/")

# Summary

print("K-MEANS CLUSTERING COMPREHENSIVE EXAMPLES - SUMMARY")
```
